newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria police clashes with protesters.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria police clashes with protesters.

text.p: Around a dozen Bulgarians were injured in a clash with riot police outside parliament in the capital Sofia on Friday as thousands demonstrated against the Socialist government.
Protesters scuffled with policemen guarding Socialist deputy and ex-interior minister Lyubomir Nachev as he left parliament, an eyewitness said. Several were hit by police clubs.
"One demonstrator walked into parliament with a bleeding wound on his head where he was treated," state radio said.
In the scuffle protesters hurled chunks of ice, stones and garbage cans at the policemen, who appeared to suffer no injury. Windows of the nearby Sofia-Grand Hotel restaurant were smashed.
Sofia mayor Stefan Sofianski arrived to attempt to restore calm, urging protesters and police to refrain from violence. A group of about 100 more riot policemen moved in as reinforcement.

As nationwide protests organised by the opposition Union of Democratic Forces went into a fifth day, UDF deputies walked out of parliament after the ruling Socialists rejected a vote on their "salvation declaration" which called for early elections.

The Bulgarian Socialist Party (BSP), formed by leading Communists after the collapse of one-party rule in 1989, had proposed to insert in the declaration parts of a Socialist declaration submitted on Thursday.

Thousands of protesters, burning red flags, marched to the parliament demanding early elections, led by a Gypsy orchestra. "The prime minister is a policeman, the country is a labour camp," read one placard.
A human chain, mostly of students, surrounded parliament, which was heavily guarded by riot police. Hundreds of taxis cruised central Sofia sounding their horns to show support.
Whistle-blowing students snowballed Socialist deputies trying to leave the building.
Demonstrators chanted "Resign" and "Elections" and burned an effigy of an old woman, representing the Socialist Party.
Several windows of the parliament building were smashed. Parallel protests are being held in several other big cities.
"The opposition is prepared to quit parliament in the next days and join the people on the streets to press for early elections," UDF leader Ivan Kostov told reporters in parliament.
Leaders of the four opposition parties represented in parliament met speaker Blagovest Sendov and outgoing Interior Minister Nikolai Dobrev.
On Wednesday the Socialists had nominated the powerful Dobrev as prime minister in place of outgoing Zhan Videnov, who resigned on December 21 after severe criticism of his management of the economy.
A report by the private radio station Darik said Dobrev had attempted to leave parliament but his jeep ran over the leg of a protester who had lain down in its path.
Dobrev was forced to return to the building after coming under a volley of snowballs.
The opposition says the BSP has failed to tackle the country's economic crisis and now lacks support to form a government.
"The BSP, which led the country to its gravest crisis in history, has no right to rule," said Yordan Sokolov, head of the UDF parliamentary group.
Three injured policeman were brought into the parliamentary building for treatment. Riot police were instructed not to use their clubs.

Opposition leaders appealed to the protesters through loudspeakers to retreat from the doors of parliament as Speaker Blagovest Sendov called an extraordinary session to discuss the situation around the assembly.
Ivan Kostov, leader of the opposition Union of Democratic Forces (UDF), welcomed the announcement of the extraordinary session, declaring: "We won."

As nationwide protests organised by the opposition Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) went into a fifth day, UDF deputies had walked out of parliament after the ruling Socialists rejected the vote on the "salvation declaration".
